project.name: jpx
project.description: A javascript image processing library toolkit
project.author: Maxime Daisy

jipl.name: jipl
jipl.description:
jipl stands for Javascript Image Processing Language. It provides a specific syntax to make image processing tasks easier, and more efficient.

Loops

`foreach(position p) in image`

Loops over image pixel positions. ```javascript foreach(position p) in image // Do something with p.x, p.y /foreach ```

`foreach(channel c) in image`

Loops over image channels. ```javascript foreach(channel c) in image // Do something with c /foreach ```

`foreach(pixel p) in image`

Loops over all image pixels. ```javascript foreach(pixel p) in image // Do something with p.x, p.y, p.c, p.index /foreach ```

Helpers

`@` as `this.`

Within a function, you can use the symbol `@` that aliases "`this.`". Example: ```javascript var image = new jpx.Image('my/super/image.png',function() { foreach(pixel p) in this var index = index; var value = `@`data[index]; // this.data[index] `@`data[index] = value / 2 + 10 * p.c; /foreach }); ```

params.name: jipl
params.description: The script to be compiled

return.description: Javascript code resulting of the compilation

classitems.description:
[ BROWSER ONLY ]

Compile each jipl script within the page. `jpx-jipl` scripts must have type `text/jpx-jipl`.
classitems.name: run
example:
<script type="text/jpx-jipl">
			var I = new jpx.Image('my/super/image.jpg', function()
			{
				foreach(pixel p) in this
					var i = p.index;
					var d = `@`data[i];
					`@`data[i] = d / 2;
				/foreach
			});
		</script>
		<script>
			jpx.jipl.run();
		</script>
